units.title: Mechanics
units.blurb: Throws, collisions, loops, circles and springs, each problem a chain of two to four linked questions.

units.title: Heat and Gases
units.blurb: A gas under a piston and a gas running an engine cycle: the gas law, work, heat and efficiency.

units.title: Waves and Sound
units.blurb: Two speakers in step, a siren near a wall and a string over a pulley: path difference, the Doppler effect and standing waves.

units.title: Light and Optics
units.blurb: A convex lens, a lamp under water and light through two slits.

units.title: Electricity and Magnetism
units.blurb: A capacitor in a circuit, beams bent by electric and magnetic fields, and a rod sliding on rails.

units.title: Atoms and Light
units.blurb: Light knocking electrons out of a metal, and hydrogen atoms jumping between energy levels.

topics.title: A Ball Thrown From a Cliff
topics.short: Split the flight into a steady sideways part and a falling part, then use energy for the landing speed.
topics.trouble: Students use the full launch speed in the vertical equation instead of its vertical component.

topics.title: A Kick Over a Wall
topics.short: Find when the ball reaches the wall from the sideways motion, then its height and direction at that moment.
topics.trouble: Students assume a ball at a wall must still be rising, without checking the sign of the vertical velocity.

topics.title: A Collision, Then a Ramp
topics.short: Momentum through the collision, energy after it: the carts stick, lose kinetic energy, then climb a ramp.
topics.trouble: Students use energy conservation across a sticking collision, where kinetic energy is lost.

topics.title: Around a Loop
topics.short: Energy gives the speed at the top of a loop; the circle's force equation gives the push of the track.
topics.trouble: Students treat the normal force at the top of a loop as pointing up, or leave out gravity in the centripetal sum.

topics.title: A Ball Swinging in a Circle
topics.short: A ball on a string sweeps a cone: the tension's vertical part holds it up, its sideways part turns it.
topics.trouble: Students use the string length as the radius of the circle instead of L sin θ.

topics.title: A Block on a Spring
topics.short: Period, top speed and timing for a block oscillating on a spring.
topics.trouble: Students think a bigger amplitude makes the period longer.

topics.title: Down a Rough Ramp Into a Spring
topics.short: Friction takes energy on the ramp; what is left squeezes a spring.
topics.trouble: Students use mg instead of mg cos θ for the normal force on the ramp.

topics.title: Gas Under a Weighted Piston
topics.short: Balance the piston to find the gas pressure, then heat the gas at that pressure.
topics.trouble: Students forget the air pressure above the piston and use only Mg/A.

topics.title: A Gas Engine Cycle
topics.short: Work as the area of a cycle, heat taken in on each leg, and the engine's efficiency.
topics.trouble: Students divide the work by all the heat exchanged, including heat given out.

topics.title: Two Speakers in Step
topics.short: Path difference decides loud or quiet; then find the frequencies that make a spot quiet.
topics.trouble: Students compare the distances themselves instead of their difference.

topics.title: A Siren Near a Wall
topics.short: A moving siren, its echo from a wall, and the beats between them.
topics.trouble: Students put the source's speed on the wrong side of the formula, or forget the wall re-sends the frequency it receives.

topics.title: A String Over a Pulley
topics.short: A hanging mass sets the wave speed; the length and the number of loops set the frequency.
topics.trouble: Students think the wave speed is proportional to the tension rather than its square root.

topics.title: An Object and a Convex Lens
topics.short: The lens equation, the image's size and kind, and what happens when the object moves.
topics.trouble: Students flip the sign of the image distance or mix up real and virtual images.

topics.title: A Lamp at the Bottom of a Pool
topics.short: Snell's law out of the water, the critical angle, and the bright circle on the surface.
topics.trouble: Students measure angles from the surface instead of from the normal.

topics.title: Light Through Two Slits
topics.short: Fringe spacing, where the bright and dark fringes fall, and how the pattern changes.
topics.trouble: Students count dark fringes like bright ones, missing the half wavelength.

topics.title: A Circuit With a Capacitor
topics.short: An uncharged capacitor acts like a wire; a full one passes no current.
topics.trouble: Students think current flows through a fully charged capacitor.

topics.title: A Beam Between Charged Plates
topics.short: A charge crossing a uniform field moves like a projectile: steady across, accelerated sideways.
topics.trouble: Students use the voltage itself as the field, forgetting to divide by the plate gap.

topics.title: A Particle Bent by a Magnetic Field
topics.short: A voltage speeds an ion up; a magnetic field bends it into a half circle that sorts by mass.
topics.trouble: Students think the radius grows in proportion to the mass, forgetting the speed depends on mass too.

topics.title: A Rod Sliding on Rails
topics.short: A moving rod makes an emf, the current feels a force, and someone has to keep pulling.
topics.trouble: Students get the current's direction backward: the induced current always opposes the motion.

topics.title: Light on a Metal Plate
topics.short: Photon energy, the fastest electrons and the stopping voltage.
topics.trouble: Students think brighter light gives faster electrons.

topics.title: Jumps Between Energy Levels
topics.short: Level energies, the photon from a jump, its wavelength and how many lines a gas can give.
topics.trouble: Students use the energy of one level instead of the difference between two.
